That there is absolutely no evidence in this record that they had any idea of who was operating the back center. This is not the situation where a patient walked into a hospital and thought the doctor with the hospital tag was its agent. This is not anything like that situation. There just was no evidence of reliance, actions by Brevard Orthopedic or anything that creates an apparent agency. As far as the undisputed evidence, and this is, again, Judge Erp was, he didn't equivocate and said, I'm thoroughly convinced of what the undisputed evidence shows. And that is Brevard Orthopedic at the time of the medical treatment was not providing medical care to patients. It didn't have physician employees, it had no income, it had no contracts with insurance carriers, it had no contracts with Medicare. It was just an entity that had assigned all of its employment contracts to Osler Medical, Inc. That is undisputed. And in fact, we know that happened because the record has evidence that Osler Medical, Inc. was paying Dr. Ismailodeh. Dr. Ismailodeh was reporting Osler Medical, Inc. to the IRS as his employer. It controlled Dr. Ismailodeh's actions. As far as just common law agency, we certainly don't have any elements, any of the three elements of agency in this record. Again, this is what after hearing all of the evidence, Judge Erp said, I'm thoroughly convinced, this is the undisputed evidence, Brevard Orthopedic assigned all of its control, everything to Osler Medical. And with that, it stopped being the business of operating as the back center treating patients. So that is undisputed, is that Brevard Orthopedic, once it assigned those contracts for the period of time until it got the employees back in June of 2011, had absolutely no say in the dealings of Osler Medical. And in fact, Dr. Hines became an employee. He was the former president. He had been the president of Brevard Orthopedic. He became the medical director of the back center and Osler Medical, an employee of Osler Medical, Inc. And that's how the decisions were made. As far as the record, there is just no inference that it was anything other than that. Some of the contracts and things, the evidence that was provided at the hearing was completely unauthenticated. But having said that, the judge did hear the evidence. He allowed proffers and the evidence didn't show anything else. So this is, again, there might've been confusion in the beginning of the case when this was first prevented to the predecessor judge as far as using the fictitious name, the back center. I think that's what caused the confusion because we know that Brevard Orthopedic now is the back center and that's how they've been assigned on the style of the case. And that's correct. But at the time of the negligence in question, the back center was Osler Medical, Inc. There's just nothing in the record to dispute that. So judge Earp heard the evidence. He heard extensive arguments. He considered everything. And again, this was a situation where he didn't say this was a close call. He didn't say he didn't equivocate. He said, I am thoroughly convinced that the undisputed evidence shows that it was Osler Medical that was employing Dr. Smiloday. And so that was a correct ruling. There's nothing else in this record really to talk about as far as the undisputed evidence. So with that, Brevard Orthopedic would ask the court to affirm the proper summary judgment that was entered in its favor. Thank you, your honors.
